construct: As fetal type II pneumocytes mature, pulmonary surfactant production rises. Lecithin (phosphatidylcholine), a major surfactant phospholipid, increases substantially late in gestation relative to sphingomyelin. The amniotic-fluid lecithin/sphingomyelin ratio is therefore a historical biochemical marker of fetal lung maturity, although routine clinical use has declined.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Advancing type II pneumocyte maturation increases surfactant phosphatidylcholine/lecithin relative to sphingomyelin, so the L/S ratio rises.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: An isolated rise in sphingomyelin can look like biochemical maturation, but the classic maturation signal is the late rise in lecithin relative to comparatively stable sphingomyelin.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The keyed relationship is the unique biochemical direction consistent with advancing surfactant maturation; the stem deliberately avoids using this historical test to decide delivery timing.
